paper.title: Fast UCB-type algorithms for stochastic bandits with heavy and super heavy symmetric noise

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with heavy / super-heavy symmetric noise
unmapped: noise is symmetric about the location mu_i with a density
only an alpha-th absolute moment bound E|xi|^alpha <= sigma^alpha with alpha > 0 (possibly alpha < 1, so the mean may not exist; mu_i is the centre of symmetry)
settings.definition_quote: For any arm $i$ ($i=1,\dots,K$) and any round $t$ ($t=1, \dots, T$), random reward $X_i^t = \mu_i + \xi_i^t$ and the probability density function $\rho_i^t$ of the noise $\xi_i^t$ satisfy the following condition: $\rho_i^t(u) = \rho_i(u)$ (i.i.d.), $\rho(u) = \rho(-u)$ (symmetric noise), there are $\sigma > 0$ and $\alpha>0$, such that $\EE[|\xi_i^t|^{\alpha}] \leq \sigma^{\alpha}$ (heavy tail).

symbols.g_inv: inverse in k of the high-probability optimization-error bound g(k, delta) of the underlying first-order algorithm

conditions: the inner first-order algorithm is g(k,delta)-bounding for f_i(x) = (x-mu_i)^2/2 with stochastic gradient oracle x - xi

source.label: thm:FO_UCB
source.quote: The regret of the \algname{FO-UCB} with $g(k, \delta)$-bounded first-order algorithm for the MAB problem with $K$ arms, auxiliary functions $f_i(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x-\mu_i)^2$, period $T$, $\delta=\frac{1}{T^2}$ satisfies $R_T \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i>0} \Delta_i (g^{-1}(\frac{\Delta_i^2}{8}, \frac{1}{T^2}) + 2)$

results.notes: Generic reduction; appendix restatement uses delta = 1/(T(T+1)) and '+1' instead of '+2'. Noise assumptions enter only via g.

symbols.g_inv: inverse in k of the high-probability optimization-error bound g(k, delta) of the underlying zero-order algorithm

conditions: the inner algorithm is g(k,delta)-bounding for f_i(x) = |x-mu_i| with zero-order oracle |x - xi|

source.label: thm:ZO_UCB
source.quote: The regret of the \algname{ZO-UCB} with $g(k, \delta)$-bounded first-order algorithm for the MAB problem with $K$ arms, auxiliary functions $f_i(x) = |x-\mu_i|$, period $T$, $\delta=\frac{1}{T^2}$ satisfies $R_T = \sum_{i=1}^K \Delta_i ( g^{-1}(\frac{\Delta_i}{2}, \frac{1}{T^2} ) + 2)$

results.notes: Paper writes '=' but proof gives an upper bound; recorded as upper bound. Statement says 'first-order' though ZO-UCB uses zero-order oracle.

symbols.C_const: constant from clipped-SGD analysis (C = 5400 sigma^2, sigma^2 variance bound of aggregated gradient estimator, Assumption 5)
symbols.R_0: upper bound on |x_0 - mu_i|, initial distance of estimate

conditions: aggregated gradient estimator satisfies Assumption 5 (bounded variance sigma^2)
tuning: batch size b=(2m+1)n with smoothed median of means

source.label: thm:MAB_theorem
source.quote: The regret of the \algname{Clipped-SGD-UCB} for multi-armed bandit problem with $K$ arms, period $T$, ... and symmetric distribution of rewards satisfies: $R_T \leq 4\log((T+1)TR^2)\sqrt{C \log(4T(T+1)^2)TK} +  \sum_i \Delta_i$

results.notes: Statement is loose: K in the tuning denotes iteration count of clipped-SGD, not arms; proof has an extra log T factor that disappears. Abstract summarises as O(log T sqrt(KT log T)).

conditions: aggregated gradient estimator satisfies Assumption 5 (bounded variance sigma^2)
results.notes: Paper writes log(4T(T+1^2)), interpreted as typo for log(4T(T+1)^2) as in the other bound.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit with heavy-tailed rewards, E|X|^{1+alpha} <= sigma^{1+alpha}, alpha in (0,1]
